questions.subject: h2-physics
questions.stem:
A child of mass m sits on a car seat which is accelerating horizontally at 0.50 g (where g is the acceleration of free fall).

What is the magnitude of the total force F exerted by the car seat on the child?
questions.stemText: A child of mass m sits on a car seat which is accelerating horizontally at 0.50 g (where g is the acceleration of free fall). F What is the magnitude of the total force F exerted by the car seat on the child? A 0.50 mg B 1.0 mg C 1.1 mg D 1.5 mg

appearances.originalFile: ACJC Physics/H2/2026 J2 H2 Physics Prelim P1 sharing.pdf

questions.difficultyReason: Requires seeing that the seat supplies both the vertical support and the horizontal accelerating force, then combining vectors.
questions.misconception: Taking only the horizontal or only the vertical component of the contact force

explanation.body:
The seat must provide a vertical component $mg$ (to balance weight) and a horizontal component $ma = 0.50\,mg$ (to accelerate the child).

$F = \sqrt{(mg)^2 + (0.50\,mg)^2} = \sqrt{1.25}\,mg \approx 1.1\,mg$.

perOption.A: This is only the horizontal component that accelerates the child.
perOption.B: This is only the vertical component that balances the weight.
perOption.C: Correct. Vector sum of $mg$ and $0.50\,mg$ is $1.1\,mg$.
perOption.D: Adds the two perpendicular components as scalars instead of as vectors.
